archetype.name: Near Miss (record outran the margin)
archetype.definition: Texas finished one game behind Houston in the AL West, but a negative run differential and nearly four wins of close-game luck mean the race was closer than the team was good.

report.headline: One game short of the West, with wins the run differential never earned

recap.finish: 80-82, second in the AL West one game behind HOU; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a .500-ish team in a division that let a .500-ish team contend. Houston took the West at 81-81, so the Rangers' 80-82 left them a single win from at least forcing the issue. The margin underneath that record was worse than the record. Texas was outscored 719 to 673 over the season, -0.28 runs per game (21st of 30). Its W vs Run Diff of +3.9 says a team with that margin usually wins about 76 games. Being in the race at all was partly borrowed.

The season had no real surge and no real collapse. A 4-1 March gave way to an 11-15 April. The best month, a 16-11 June, came while the team was being outscored 113-123. July was the worst stretch: 136 runs allowed in 24 games, the most of any month, and an 11-13 record. August (13-15) and September (12-12) treaded water. The longest winning and losing streaks were both six games. The last ten went 4-6, including 2-10 and 4-6 losses at Minnesota in the final series, at a point where one more win would have matched Houston.

The offense ranked 25th in runs per game and posted a .713 OPS (20th). The park, with a factor of 88, suppresses scoring and explains part of that, and several regulars graded above average once park-adjusted. Ezequiel Duran carried the group: 4.4 WAR, 109 wRC+ and 12.7 Def Runs, third on the third-base tab. Josh Jung (136 wRC+) and Joc Pederson (128 wRC+, 26 HR) were the best bats. Wyatt Langford added a 115 wRC+ but played only 110 games. Two spots dragged the group to a C+. Evan Carter got 455 plate appearances with a 74 wRC+. Logan O'Hoppe posted a 63 wRC+ and -0.9 WAR as a DH, a position where the bat is the only job.

The bigger story is run prevention sliding back. In 2025 Texas allowed the fewest runs in the league with a 3.47 ERA. This year the staff's ERA rose to 4.32 (22nd), and the team fell to 14th in runs allowed. In a park that favors pitchers, that is a real drop. The rotation's B- grade and its FIP numbers suggest some of it was bad sequencing rather than bad pitching. Jacob deGrom struck out 30.1% of batters with a 3.11 FIP, yet his ERA was 4.20. MacKenzie Gore's 3.87 FIP sat well below his 4.58 ERA. Jack Leiter (5.29 ERA) was the weak link before landing on the 60-day IL. The bullpen graded C around an All-Star closer. Jacob Latz had 30 saves and a 2.13 ERA, but Chase Silseth walked 12.9% of the hitters he faced in a high-leverage role.

Put together, it is the third straight year of the same team: 78-84, 81-81, 80-82, finishing 17th on the site the last two seasons. Last year it underperformed its run differential by nine wins. This year it beat a worse differential by four. The two errors roughly cancel, and the underlying club has been drifting from slightly good to slightly bad.

highlights.title: Duran's two-way season at third
highlights.body: Duran led the team with 4.4 WAR. He paired a 109 wRC+ with 12.7 Def Runs over 153 games, and the defense is what lifted him to third on his position's tab. Fielding value swings year to year, but he played every day and contributed on both sides.

highlights.title: deGrom pitched better than his ERA
highlights.body: deGrom's 30.1% strikeout rate, 6.9% walk rate and 3.11 FIP point to a front-line starter. His 4.20 ERA is the kind of gap that tends to close in a pitcher's favor. Over 162.2 innings he produced 4.3 WAR, the most on the staff.

highlights.title: Latz anchored the ninth
highlights.body: Latz made the All-Star team with 30 saves and a 2.13 ERA. His 30.6% strikeout rate and 2.84 FIP support the result. He was the one clearly reliable piece of a C-grade bullpen.

lowlights.title: Run prevention gave back last year's edge
lowlights.body: The staff ERA rose from 3.47 in 2025 to 4.32, and the team slipped from first to 14th in runs allowed. July's 136 runs allowed was the low point. Starter FIPs below their ERAs suggest part of this reverses, but the staff is no longer the league's best.

lowlights.title: Two lineup holes sank the offense
lowlights.body: Carter (74 wRC+ in 455 PA) and O'Hoppe (63 wRC+, -0.9 WAR in 274 PA) took nearly 730 plate appearances of well-below-average offense. That contributed to a lineup that ranked 25th in runs per game despite several above-average regulars.

lowlights.title: The record was propped up by luck
lowlights.body: Texas was outscored by 0.28 runs per game, yet a +3.9 W vs Run Diff kept it in the race. June's 16-11 record came despite being outscored. Close-game edges like this rarely carry over.

arc.note: After a quick start the Rangers hovered within a few games of .500 every month. A lucky June was their only push, and a 4-6 finish left them one game behind Houston.

recap.nextYear: The core that carried the year is identifiable. Duran's two-way value, Jung's and Pederson's bats and deGrom's peripherals all grade well, and Langford was productive when he played. The rotation's B- grade and its FIP-ERA gaps argue it is better than its 4.32 ERA. The bullpen beyond Latz is ordinary, and Silseth's walk rate is a concern. The lineup needs real production from the Carter and O'Hoppe plate appearances. The warning sign is the margin: a negative run differential plus nearly four lucky wins describes a team closer to 76 wins than 80. Three straight seasons near .500 suggest this roster, as constituted, sits in the middle of the league rather than on the edge of a title.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the luck read rests on a full-year run differential.
